newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Wednesday sold steady to $1.00 per cwt lower amid light packer demand and more than adequate hog supplies, livestock dealers said.
"At the rate that hogs are moving, we should have Friday's supplies lined up by the end of the day," one interior Iowa and southern Minnesota packer hog buyer said.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 lower at $55.00 to $56.00 in the country and $56.50 to $57.00 at plants, with a few possible at $57.50, dealers said.
Illinois hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 lower at $55.50 to $56.00 in the country and $56.50 to $57.50 at plants, with a few loads possible at $58.00, central Illinois dealers said.
Indiana hogs sold $1.00 lower at $55.50 in the country and $57.00, with a few $57.75 at plants.
"Its pretty slow right now, and I'm not sure we know the bottom yet," an Indiana source said.
Ohio hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower, with a top of $56.00 in the country and $57.00 at plants.
